title: Model Photos Without a Photoshoot | AIVideosUGC
description: Get model photos without a photoshoot: photograph the garment flat, pick an adult look and setting, then check the fit before posting. Learn how and try it.
h1: How to Get Model Photos Without a Photoshoot
lead: You can get model photos without a photoshoot. Photograph the garment flat, then pick an adult look you can save and reuse. Check the fit details before you post.
secondary_keywords: on-model photos from a flat lay
summary: A flat or hanger photo becomes a photo of an adult wearing the piece. Check the neckline, length, print, and zippers before you post.

paras: When a flat photo is enough, how to photograph the garment, and how to save a look. It also covers jewelry, what to compare, several colors at once, the three steps, and the other photo tools.
sections.alt: Adult man with short silver hair wearing a plain gray hoodie outside a storefront.

sections.h2: Put Your Products on an AI Model
paras: These photos fit a new arrival, a few pieces, or print on demand (made after the order). Booking a model, a photographer, and a studio day is a lot to arrange for that.

You upload a photo of the piece, pick who wears it and where, and get a photo of it being worn. These photos do not prove the exact fit. A generated image cannot show how a medium size will fit a shopper. Keep the size chart and the measurements on the listing.
sections.alt: Adult woman with short copper hair wearing a plain gray hoodie on an autumn city sidewalk.

sections.h2: Launch New Arrivals Without a Studio Day
paras: Lay the piece flat, or hang it on a bare wall. Photograph it from the front, in daylight, and steam the wrinkles out first. Once that photo exists, a new arrival can go on an adult look.

Creases in that photo can turn into odd folds on the person. Get the whole garment in the picture, including the sleeves, the hem, and the collar. Turn a print toward the camera. Photograph each color on its own. A generated color may not match the real garment. For photos that are not on a person, the [AI product photo generator](page:photo-hub) covers other angles and close details.
sections.alt: Hands smooth a plain gray hoodie beside a wooden hanger on a light surface.

sections.h2: Keep One Look Across Every Channel
paras: Save the adult look, the pose, and the scene. On the next piece, pick that saved look so the face stays the same.

Use the same saved look on the product page, a [marketplace listing](page:plat-amazon), and an [Instagram post](page:plat-instagram). The shop then does not switch to a different person. If you describe someone new each time, the face can change. Repeat the age, the hair, and the body type so the pictures feel like one set. A linen dress might be a woman in her forties on a sunny path, in late-day light. A hoodie might be a young man by a brick wall, hands in the front pocket, in cloudy daylight. Do not ask for a celebrity, or for someone meant to look like a famous person. Those requests may be refused. On the product page, put a plain product photo first, then the photos of the piece being worn.

sections.h2: Can I make AI jewelry model photos the same way?
paras: Yes. Use a close, sharp photo of the piece on a plain surface. Keep the clasp, the stones, and the chain easy to see. Save the look if the next piece should be on the same person.

A short line you type is enough. For example: a close side view, short hair back, soft window light, and the earring easy to see. In the result, count the stones and check the clasp. See whether a necklace hangs where that length should. Small pieces need a sharper photo than clothing does.
The photo can show how the cloth hangs, where a print sits, and how a neckline looks on a body. It still does not prove a size. Keep the size chart on the listing.

Compare each image with the real piece. Check the neckline, the sleeve and hem length, where the print sits, the number of buttons, and which side the zipper is on. Stripes and plaid should line up the way they do on the garment. Give the hands and the hairline a second look. If anything does not match, make a new version. Do not post one that is only close. Plan two or three images per piece. Use one full view, one closer photo of the cloth or the stone, and one in a setting that fits how it is worn. Each image costs 24 credits. Credits are the points in your plan, and the cost is shown before you start. Files come out square, the same width and height, which fits a product gallery. For a feed post, the [AI ad image generator](page:social-ad-photos) can turn a photo you already reviewed into a square ad image. Different ages and body types are available. Pick the ones that match who you sell to.
sections.alt: Adult East Asian man checking the sleeve and hem of a plain gray hoodie in a fitting room.

sections.h2: Make the Whole Color Set Together
paras: When one arrival has more than one color, run a batch. A batch is several photos at once, with the same saved look and the same scene. Review every file before it goes on the site.

Pair the worn photos with a flat photo from the [photo tools](page:photo-hub). Add a room scene from [lifestyle photos](page:lifestyle-photos). Add a plain backdrop from the [background tool](page:change-background). A new color belongs on the [color variant](page:tpl-color) page. A variant is another color of the same piece. Compare it with the real garment before you use it. [Fashion listings](page:ind-fashion-clothing) can use the same saved look across the collection.

Pick an adult look and a scene, and save that look if you will reuse it. The clothes come from your photo.
Download the square photo. Check the neckline, length, print, and zippers against the real piece.

faq.q: How does a photo of someone wearing the piece get made?
faq.a: You upload a flat or hanger photo, pick an adult look and a scene, and download a square image of the piece being worn. Then you compare it with the real garment.

faq.q: Can I put my own products on a generated person?
faq.a: Yes. The clothing or jewelry comes from your photo. You pick the person, the pose, and the light. Do not ask for a celebrity, or for someone meant to look like a famous person.

faq.q: Will the same person appear in all my photos?
faq.a: Yes, if you save the look and pick it again. If you describe someone new each time, the face can change. Repeat the age, hair, and build when you want the set to feel related.

faq.q: How close is this to a studio shoot?
faq.a: It shows the piece on a person, in a scene you pick. It does not measure how a size will fit a shopper. Keep the size chart and the measurements on the listing. Check the neckline, length, print, and zippers.

faq.q: Can a catalog send these photos through the API?
faq.a: Yes. A catalog can send products through the API and get the photos back. The API lets your shop's own system send that work. Each image is still 24 credits, and the cost is shown before it starts.

faq.q: Do I need to say the person in the photo is generated?
faq.a: Check the current disclosure rule for the platform or marketplace where the image will appear. Rules differ by site and change, so follow the current one rather than an old screenshot.

faq.q: What photo should I start from?
faq.a: Use a sharp, front-facing photo with the whole garment visible. Smooth wrinkles and use even light so fabric, print, and trim are easy to review.

faq.q: Can the image prove a garment fits?
faq.a: No. It cannot show how a size will sit on a shopper. Keep your size chart and measurements on the listing.

faq.q: How many credits does one photo of the piece on a person use?
faq.a: One photo uses 24 credits, the points in your plan. The cost shows before you start. If it fails, the credits come back.

faq.q: Can I use jewelry as well as clothing?
faq.a: Yes. Start with a close photo that shows the clasp, stones, and chain, then check those details in the result.

faq.q: How should I review the result?
faq.a: Compare it with the real piece. Check the neckline, sleeve and hem length, print position, buttons, zipper side, clasp, stones, hands, and hairline.

faq.q: Can I make all the colors together?
faq.a: Yes. Save the look, and run a batch (several colors at once). Review each file. A generated color may not match the real garment, so compare them.
